summary: The toy shows the stages of apoptosis as a pathology review describes them: shrinkage, condensed chromatin, blebbing, a broken-up nucleus and membrane-bound apoptotic bodies. The clearing of the bodies and the neighbor that moves in are simplified.

claims.claim: Early in apoptosis the cell shrinks and its chromatin condenses (pyknosis).
claims.how: The whole cell scales down to 82 percent; the nucleus shrinks and darkens as a condensed copy fades in.

sources.title: Apoptosis: a review of programmed cell death (Toxicologic Pathology 35:495-516, 2007)
sources.says: During the early process of apoptosis, cell shrinkage and pyknosis are visible by light microscopy … Pyknosis is the result of chromatin condensation.

claims.claim: The plasma membrane blebs, then the nucleus breaks up (karyorrhexis) and the cell separates into apoptotic bodies.
claims.how: Two sets of blebs bulge in turn; the nucleus is replaced by four dark pieces; the membrane pinches into seven spheres that become solid pieces.

sources.title: Apoptosis: a review of programmed cell death (Toxicologic Pathology 35:495-516, 2007)
sources.says: Extensive plasma membrane blebbing occurs followed by karyorrhexis and separation of cell fragments into apoptotic bodies.

claims.claim: Apoptotic bodies are wrapped in intact membrane and hold tightly packed organelles, some with a piece of the nucleus.
claims.how: Each body is a membrane shell with the mitochondria and vesicles that were in its part of the cell; the middle one holds the nuclear pieces.

sources.title: Apoptosis: a review of programmed cell death (Toxicologic Pathology 35:495-516, 2007)
sources.says: Apoptotic bodies consist of cytoplasm with tightly packed organelles with or without a nuclear fragment.

claims.claim: The bodies are cleared by phagocytes, with essentially no inflammation.
claims.how: The bodies drift away out of view; the About text says white blood cells eat them.

sources.title: Apoptosis: a review of programmed cell death (Toxicologic Pathology 35:495-516, 2007)
sources.says: These bodies are subsequently phagocytosed by macrophages, parenchymal cells, or neoplastic cells … There is essentially no inflammatory reaction associated with the process of apoptosis.

claims.note: The phagocytes are not drawn; the bodies drift away instead.

simplified: The cell is a diagram: a few mitochondria and vesicles stand for its organelles.
The blebs come and go in two alternating sets, as a regular pattern.
The bodies drift away rather than being eaten, and a neighbor of the same kind moves in, so the toy can play again.
Apoptosis takes minutes to hours; the toy takes about 14 seconds.
